discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moire quantum matter)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and van der Waals quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees would produce nearly flat electronic bands, where interactions dominate kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this experimentally. Using a tear-and-stack technique for precise angle control, they reported correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. Their work turned the twist angle into a new control parameter for quantum matter. It started the field of moire materials, in which Mott physics, orbital magnetism, Chern insulators and, more recently, fractional quantum anomalous Hall states are realised and tuned electrostatically in one device. These are rigorous low-temperature transport experiments of exceptional cleanliness, and they changed how condensed-matter physicists everywhere design and probe strongly correlated electron systems. Laboratories around the world, including in India, now build on this platform.
